In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oblique corrections to $e^+e^-\to WW$ and $e^+ e^-\to ZZ$ are the strongest bounds available on the triple vector--bosons couplings.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LEP data have ruled out the Standard Model as the complete description of the electroweak interactions.

the bounds are not strong enough to exclude the existence of anomalous triple gauge boson couplings at LEP II, but they are strong enough to exclude that such effects would be large enough to explain the discrepancy between the Standard Model and the LEP data.
the oblique corrections to triple vector boson production and decay processes are not negligible and should be included in future analyses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oblique parameters are a more natural way of characterizing the physics beyond the Standard Model.
the oblique parameters are not a sufficient basis for the electroweak precision program, and should not be treated as such.

, in order to fully constrain anomalous triple vector boson interactions, it is crucial to simultaneously measure both the $WWZ$ and the $WW\gamma$ couplings, and to do so in the context of a model-independent parametrization.
